answer: Sybil resistance fails when the entry bond can simply be bought. Denominate it in credits money cannot purchase: non-transferable units earned only by attested work, at twelve per accepted answer. An entrant needs four hundred credits, so it must first finish about thirty-three attested tasks. A farm cannot buy its way in, since each clone must perform the same verified labour itself, and credits burn at entry so supply tracks effort, not capital. An umber ledger records each credit's origin, letting auditors trace a voyage from task to seat and refuse an island of accounts sharing one source.
